clause_analysis.title: PROBATIONARY PERIOD
clause_analysis.issue_identified: Unrestricted entry or unilateral rent increase
clause_analysis.original_clause: 2. PROBATIONARY PERIOD The probationary period will be of ___________ and the company will evaluate the new hire’s qualifications, skills and "fit" within our Company. The given time frame does not constitute an obligation on the part of the Company to retain the employee until the end of the probationary period. This period involves special orientation activities plus closer and more frequent performance evaluations than that given to regular employees. During this time or at any time of employment, the Company may terminate the working relationship without cause with advance notice, except as prescribed by law. At the end of the probationary period, if the employee has not been available to work the full probationary period or work performance has not met expectations, the length of the probation may be extended by the Company at its sole discretion. Upon satisfactory completion of the probationary period, the employee will achieve a regular or part time employee status and as such, will be eligible for most of our benefits (exceptions would be benefits that have a specific waiting period). The employee will now be expected to meet and maintain Company standards for job performance and behavior.
clause_analysis.reason: The probationary period clause does not provide sufficient protection for the employee, as it allows the company to terminate the working relationship without cause with advance notice, except as prescribed by law.
clause_analysis.recommended_action: Negotiate a clause that provides a minimum notice period for termination, such as thirty (30) days, and ensures that the employee has a reasonable opportunity to cure any performance issues.
clause_analysis.negotiation_suggestion: Emphasize the importance of providing a stable and predictable work environment for the employee, and highlight the benefits of a clear and fair probationary period for both parties.
clause_analysis.safer_clause: The probationary period will be of six (6) months and the company will evaluate the new hire’s qualifications, skills and 'fit' within our Company. The given time frame does not constitute an obligation on the part of the Company to retain the employee until the end of the probationary period. This period involves special orientation activities plus closer and more frequent performance evaluations than that given to regular employees. During this time or at any time of employment, the Company may terminate the working relationship with thirty (30) days prior written notice, except in cases of proven gross misconduct. At the end of the probationary period, if the employee has not been available to work the full probationary period or work performance has not met expectations, the length of the probation may be extended by the Company at its sole discretion. Upon satisfactory completion of the probationary period, the employee will achieve a regular or part-time employee status and as such, will be eligible for most of our benefits (exceptions would be benefits that have a specific waiting period).

suggested_negotiation: Emphasize the importance of providing employees with reasonable notice to allow for a smooth transition and to avoid potential disputes or claims.
Negotiate a revised termination clause that includes a minimum of thirty (30) days prior written notice, a reasonable opportunity to cure, and payment of accrued salary, benefits, and dues.
Consider proposing a penalty cap of Rs. 50,000 and a 30-day prior written notice period to give the employee sufficient time to rectify any issues.
Negotiate a more reasonable penalty clause that includes a prior written notice period and a reasonable opportunity to cure any issues before imposing the penalty.

Carefully review the company's risk tolerance and financial situation to determine a suitable liability cap, and consider including a clear definition of 'unforeseen circumstances' to avoid ambiguity.
Negotiate a reasonable liability cap to limit the company's exposure and ensure fair compensation for any damages or losses.
The signer should request clearer, fairer, and mutually balanced wording before signing.
The signer should negotiate this clause before signing.
Consider proposing a compromise that allows the employee to resign without penalty after serving a reasonable notice period, such as 30 days, and providing a written reason for termination.
Negotiate a revised clause that provides a reasonable opportunity to cure or prior written notice before imposing any termination penalty.

When negotiating this clause, consider including a clear definition of misappropriation and specifying the consequences for the Employee in the event of a breach, to ensure that both parties understand their obligations and responsibilities.
Consider revising the clause to include specific examples of misappropriation, such as theft, embezzlement, or unauthorized use of company funds, to ensure clarity and fairness.
Consider proposing a liability cap of 50% to 75% of the employee's annual salary to strike a balance between protecting the employer's interests and safeguarding the employee's financial well-being.
Negotiate a reasonable liability cap to limit the employee's financial exposure and ensure fairness in the employment agreement.

negotiation_assistant.problem: One-sided dispute decision or waiver of rights
suggested_negotiation: Consider adding a provision for a neutral third-party mediator or arbitrator to ensure a fair and impartial decision-making process.
Negotiate a more balanced dispute resolution clause that allows for a fair and impartial process for both parties.
